'''Assaf Naor''' ({{Langx|he|אסף נאור}}; born May 7, 1975) is an [[Israeli American]] and [[Czech Republic|Czech]] [[mathematician]], [[computer scientist]], and a professor of mathematics at [[Princeton University]].<ref>[https://web.math.princeton.edu/~naor/ Assaf Naor's home page at Princeton]</ref><ref>[https://www.ams.org/notices/201104/rtx110400603p.pdf AMS Notices - April 2011]</ref>

==Academic career==
Naor earned a baccalaureate from [[Hebrew University of Jerusalem]] in 1996 and a doctorate from the same university in 2002, under the supervision of [[Joram Lindenstrauss]].<ref name="cv">[https://web.math.princeton.edu/~naor/homepage%20files/cv-new.pdf Curriculum vitae], retrieved 2019-06-15.</ref><ref>{{mathgenealogy|id=110094}}</ref> He worked at [[Microsoft Research]] from 2002 until 2007, with an affiliated faculty position at the [[University of Washington]], and joined the NYU faculty in 2006.<ref name="cv"/>

==Research==
{{Scholia}}
Naor's research concerns [[metric space]]s, their properties, and related algorithms, including improved upper bounds on the [[Grothendieck inequality]], applications of this inequality, and research on [[metrical task system]]s.

==Awards and honors==
Naor won the Bergmann award of the [[United States – Israel Binational Science Foundation]] in 2007,<ref>[http://www.bsf.org.il/bsfpublic/DefaultPage1.aspx?PageId=311&innerTextID=311 Bergmann Memorial - List of Past Awards] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091125222326/http://www.bsf.org.il/BSFPublic/DefaultPage1.aspx?PageId=311&innerTextID=311 |date=2009-11-25 }}, BSF, retrieved 2013-02-23.</ref> and the Pazy award of the BSF in 2011.<ref>[http://www.bsf.org.il/bsfpublic/DefaultPage1.aspx?PageId=33&innerTextID=33 Professor A. Pazy Award] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190119091144/http://www.bsf.org.il/bsfpublic/DefaultPage1.aspx?PageId=33&innerTextID=33 |date=2019-01-19 }}, BSF, retrieved 2013-02-23.</ref> In 2012 he was one of four faculty winners of the [[Blavatnik Awards for Young Scientists|Leonard Blavatnik Award]] of the [[New York Academy of Sciences]], given to young scientists and engineers in New York, New Jersey, and Connecticut.<ref>[http://www.nyas.org/awards/blavatnik.aspx 2012 Blavatnik Awards for Young Scientists], NYAS, retrieved 2013-02-23.</ref>

He won the [[Salem Prize]] in 2008 for "contributions to the structural theory of metric spaces and its applications to computer science",<ref>{{Deprecated archive|url=https://archive.today/20130403081143/http://cims.nyu.edu/webapps/content/announcements/Naor_Salem|title=Assaf Naor receives the 2008 Salem Prize}}, NYU, retrieved 2013-02-23.</ref> and in the same year was given a [[European Mathematical Society]] Prize<ref name="cv"/> (one of ten awarded to outstanding younger mathematicians). He won the [[Bôcher Memorial Prize]] in 2011 "for introducing new invariants of metric spaces and for applying his new understanding of the distortion between  various metric structures to theoretical computer science".<ref>{{citation|title=2011 Bôcher Prize|date=April 2011|journal=Notices of the AMS|url=https://www.ams.org/notices/201104/rtx110400603p.pdf|pages=603–605|volume=58|issue=4}}.</ref> In 2012 he became a fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>[https://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society], retrieved 2013-02-23.</ref>
He received the [[Nemmers Prize in Mathematics]] in 2018 and in 2019 the [[Ostrowski Prize]].<ref>[https://ostrowski.ch/index_e.php?ifile= Ostrowski Prize 2019]</ref>

He gave an [[list of International Congresses of Mathematicians Plenary and Invited Speakers|invited talk at the International Congress of Mathematicians]] in 2010, on the topic of "Functional Analysis and Applications".<ref>{{cite web|title=ICM Plenary and Invited Speakers since 1897|url=http://www.mathunion.org/db/ICM/Speakers/SortedByCongress.php|publisher=[[International Congress of Mathematicians]]|access-date=2013-08-15|archive-date=2017-11-08|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171108012153/http://www.mathunion.org/db/ICM/Speakers/SortedByCongress.php|url-status=dead}}</ref>
